Texts: Using my design as a prompt. The website made complex effects that would take me a long time to code out, but only took a few minutes for AI to generate. Although after 3 improved versions of the beginning template, no matter how you prompt it, the website generated will become a mess and no longer be renderable by browsers, and it has only been released recently, I can't imagine how useful AI can be for future web developers.

Wikimedia Commons is the first web archive that comes to mind. If you don't know what it is, it stores all the images, audio, and documentation from your visits to Wikipedia.;

This web archive is attached to the main Wikipedia site, serving as a dedicated storage site. While it's still searchable within the site, the items mainly come from various entries, and are mostly academic in nature, local storage and searching are not its primary purpose.

Spunk Library is a quirky archive that focuses on the chaotic internet content from before 2000, focusing on content that was uploaded by early internet users during a time when the internet was still in disarray, lacking regulation and consensus. The archive still retains a strong old-fashioned internet style, using archaic search methods. You can also see some plain text (only text and line breaks) as records of web page content, and a series of rough but simple information archives.
